title: The Animal Is Poor in World

work.full: The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics: World, Finitude, Solitude

coverage_sections: §§45-48 (Part Two, Chapter Three): the propositional character of the thesis and the metaphysics/positive-science relation (§45); poverty-in-world vs world-formation, poverty as deprivation/Entbehrung, not hierarchy (§46); poverty-in-world vs worldlessness, world as accessibility of beings (§47); the sense in which the animal has and does not have world (§48).
spine_role: First substantive unit of Part Two's comparative animal-thesis chapter. Carries the boredom spine forward indirectly: having established (Ch.2/fcm-09) that the world-question must be opened comparatively, this unit fixes the working sense of 'world' that the whole metaphysics turns on — world = the accessibility of beings as beings — by triangulating the animal between the worldless stone and world-forming man. Poverty is recast as deprivation (Entbehrung), not lesser degree, preparing the Uexkull-grounded organism analysis of Ch.4.

sections.title: The propositional character of this thesis and the relation between metaphysics and the positive sciences; the circular movement of philosophy
The thesis 'the animal is poor in world' in relation to 'man is world-forming'; poverty/world-formation is not a hierarchical assessment; poverty in world as deprivation of world
The thesis 'the animal is poor in world' in relation to 'the stone is worldless'; worldlessness as not having access to beings; provisional characterization of world as the accessibility of beings
The sense in which the animal has and does not have world: attaining a place from which to begin the elucidation of the concept of world

key_terms.gloss: weltarm; the guiding thesis predicated of every animal as such — a statement of essence (not a generalization), hence a presupposition of zoology rather than a zoological result.
Entbehren / Entbehrung; being-poor properly means being deprived, not merely 'having less'. Poverty-in-world = a deprivation of world, not a smaller quantity of world.

Armut, etymologically heard through Mut (mood): Ar-mut / armmutig as 'in a mood of poverty', by analogy with schwermutig (melancholy) / demutig (humility); poverty is a way of comporting and bearing oneself, not a mere property.
weltlos; predicated of the stone, which has no access to beings around it; because it cannot have access it cannot even be deprived of world — worldlessness is constitutive, not a lack.
weltbildend; predicated of man, whose relation to world is richer, more extensive in penetrability, and constantly extendable in range and depth.

The provisional/working concept of world: beings which are in each case accessible and may be dealt with; later sharpened to accessibility of beings as beings. World is not quantity/sum-total/degree of accessible beings.

The positive characterization of the stone's worldlessness: 'having no access' belongs to and makes possible the stone's specific manner of being (presence-at-hand, the realm of physical-material nature).
Vorhandenheit; the stone's manner of being — it turns up here or there amongst other things but is essentially without access to them; this belongs to its being.
Wesensaussage; the thesis holds for all animals because it is essential, not essential because it holds for all — universal validity results from essential knowledge, not the reverse.
The thesis derives from zoology yet must be its presupposition; philosophy moves in a circle whose essential feature is not return-to-origin but the view of the centre that circling alone provides.

Umwelt; the Uexkull-derived term — the animal is confined to its environmental world, 'immured as it were within a fixed sphere incapable of further expansion or contraction'; the thesis seems to run counter to this familiar talk.

Illustration of differential access: cross out 'rock' to mark that what the lizard lies on is given-for-it yet not as a being/rock; the blade of grass is no blade of grass for the beetle but a 'beetle-path' for beetle-nourishment.

claims.text: The thesis 'the animal is poor in world' is a statement of essence and a presupposition of zoology, not a result of it; universal validity follows from essential knowledge, not the reverse.

The relation between metaphysics and the positive sciences is necessarily ambiguous and circular; the essential feature of philosophy's circular movement is the view of the centre that circling alone provides, not the return to a starting-point.
Metaphysics and positive research cannot be played off as two consecutive phases of one production process (one supplying facts, the other concepts); their inner unity is 'a matter of fate'.

The comparison of man and animal in terms of world-formation and poverty-in-world allows no evaluative ranking; man can sink lower than any animal, and within the animal realm amoebae are no more imperfect than apes — every animal is as perfect and complete as any other.

Being poor does not mean possessing little or less than another; being poor means being deprived (Entbehren). Poverty-in-world therefore expresses a deprivation of world, not a quantitative difference, and 'world' in the thesis cannot signify quantity, sum-total, or degree of accessible beings.

World is provisionally defined as those beings which are in each case accessible and may be dealt with; the worldlessness of the stone is its having no access to those beings (as beings) amongst which it is.

It is beside the point to regard the stone's having-no-access as a lack: having no access is precisely what makes possible its specific kind of being — the realm of physical-material nature and its laws.

Whatever the lizard lies on is given for it in some way yet is not accessible to it as a being; every animal has a specific, non-arbitrary set of relationships (nourishment, prey, enemies, mates) within an environmental world confined like a fixed sphere.

The animal both has and does not have world: if world = accessibility of beings and to live is to have access, the animal stands with man; if poverty = deprivation = not-having, it stands with the stone — contradictory by common logic, but metaphysics has a different logic.

The propositions must employ 'world' and 'accessibility' in different senses in each case; the concept of world is thereby shown to be still unclarified, and the place is identified where its elucidation (and the organism analysis) must begin.

interlocutors.name: Jakob von Uexkull
interlocutors.role: Source of the 'environmental world' (Umwelt) talk that Heidegger's thesis appears to contradict and will appropriate critically; named as having accustomed everyone to speaking of the animal's environmental world.

interlocutors.name: Max Scheler
interlocutors.role: Foil: his anthropology unifies the hierarchical sequence material being / life / spirit; Heidegger judges this a fundamental error that denies him access to metaphysics, while granting the question Scheler posed is essential and superior to prior attempts.

interlocutors.name: Hans Spemann
interlocutors.role: Named exemplar of a researcher 'of stature' whose influence on students should show not as personality-cult but as thoughtful respect; illustrates the leadership/fate of science argument.

interlocutors.name: vitalism / teleology / anti-mechanism
interlocutors.role: The contemporary slogans ('vitalism', 'the teleological perspective of life', 'the struggle against mechanism') under which biology resists physico-chemical reduction; Heidegger endorses the negative tendency but warns it is as burdened with misunderstanding as mechanism.

anchor_phrases: the animal is poor in world
poverty in world implies a deprivation of world
world as the accessibility of beings
both has and does not have world
bridge_relevance: The unit's central yield — world = the accessibility of beings as beings — is the most economical statement in FCM of world-as-disclosedness, and it is reached precisely by contrast: the stone is worldless because it has no access, the animal poor because its access is a confined deprivation, man world-forming because his access is extendable in range and depth. This accessibility/disclosure axis is what links the animal chapter back to the boredom analysis (boredom as the attunement that discloses beings-as-a-whole withdrawing) and forward to the pipeline's interest in graded openness/engagement: poverty-as-deprivation supplies a model for treating boredom not as a mere absence of stimulation (a 'less') but as a determinate mode of being-held in a restricted disclosure.
